answer.rationale: The 18% spend mandate combined with incumbent refusal to reopen pricing creates a constraint that rules out negotiation (memory_c4 shows negotiation works but only with willing counterparties) and renewal (memory_c1 shows stability but no cost relief). The 94% line utilization creates delivery risk that prevents deferral. Adding a second source (memory_c3) would help resilience but not address the 18% cost cut mandate. Switching to the low-cost vendor (memory_c2) has proven track record: quick onboarding, accurate invoicing, and sharp cost reduction. With 14 days before expiration and a single decision window, switching primary supply is the only action that directly addresses the mandate while memory_c2 evidence shows execution risk is manageable. This flags downstream value risk because it commits to a vendor change under time pressure, but the alternative—failing to meet the financial mandate—creates greater organizational risk.
